title: Composition isomorphisms of etale inverse images of sheaves of sets, with units
statement: For a morphism of schemes $e:T\to S$ and a sheaf of sets $G$ on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], $e^{-1}G$ denotes the etale inverse image of sheaves of sets: the sheafification of the presheaf $e_pG(V)=\varinjlim_{(U,\varphi)}G(U)$ on $T_{\Et}$, the colimit over the pairs of an object $U$ of $S_{\Et}$ and a $T$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U\times_ST$, i.e. $u_s$ for the functor $u:S_{\Et}\to T_{\Et}$, $U\mapsto U\times_ST$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1), of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (2) with values in sets (the construction of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] with values in sets); it is left adjoint to $e_*$, $(e_*H)(U)=H(U\times_ST)$. For an object $U$ of $S_{\Et}$ and $s\in G(U)$ write $e^*s\in(e^{-1}G)(U\times_ST)$ for the image of $s$ under the unit $G\to e_*e^{-1}G$. Let $f:Y\to X$ and $g:W\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Then for every sheaf of sets $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ there is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets $c_{f,g,F}:g^{-1}f^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}(f\circ g)^{-1}F$ on $W_{\Et}$, natural in $F$, such that: (0) (units) for every morphism $e:T\to S$, every sheaf of sets $G$ on $S_{\Et}$, every morphism $a:U'\to U$ of $S_{\Et}$ and $s\in G(U)$, $e^*(s|_{U'})=(e^*s)|_{U'\times_ST}$, and for every morphism of sheaves $\psi:G\to G'$, $e^*(\psi_U(s))=(e^{-1}\psi)(e^*s)$; (1) $c_{f,g,F}(g^*(f^*s))=(f\circ g)^*s$ for every object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ and every $s\in F(U)$, where $(U\times_XY)\times_YW$ is identified with $U\times_XW$ by the canonical isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]; and $c_{f,g,F}$ is the only morphism of sheaves $g^{-1}f^{-1}F\to(f\circ g)^{-1}F$ with this property; (2) (associativity) for a further morphism $h:V\to W$, the two isomorphisms $h^{-1}g^{-1}f^{-1}F\to(f\circ g\circ h)^{-1}F$, namely $c_{f\circ g,h,F}\circ h^{-1}(c_{f,g,F})$ and $c_{f,g\circ h,F}\circ c_{g,h,f^{-1}F}$, are equal.

proof.text: Apply naturality of the adjunction unit, first as a morphism of sheaves at a.op and then as a natural transformation at a sheaf morphism. Evaluate both equalities on a section. The adjunction is the existing sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous along the etale base-change functor; its left functor is definitionally Scheme.etaleSetPullback.

Construct setPushComp with Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp' and the inverse of MorphismProperty.Over.pullbackComp. Thus its inverse component evaluates to restriction along the inverse canonical fibre-product pasting isomorphism. These comparisons are the existing canonical fibre-product maps, not new choices.

Compose the two sheaf-pullback adjunctions with Adjunction.comp. Apply the inverse of conjugateIsoEquiv to setPushComp.symm to construct setPullComp, from iterated to composite inverse image. Mathlib unit_conjugateEquiv_symm gives its unit equation. Evaluate the equation on a site object and a section, and unfold Adjunction.comp_unit_app and the pushforward comparison to obtain exactly the stated section formula.

For a fixed sheaf F, apply injectivity of the composite adjunction homEquiv to q and the comparison component. By Adjunction.homEquiv_unit their images are the composites of the iterated unit with the composite right adjoint applied to the two maps. Extensionality on site objects and sections identifies these images: the assumed section equation for q and the proven section equation for setPullComp have the same right hand side. Hence q equals the comparison. This does not require local generation or the sheaf axiom.

Prove setPullComp_conjugate by the inverse law for conjugateIsoEquiv. Conjugate the desired associativity equality of inverse comparison isomorphisms under the triple adjunction. The proved source-library conjugateIsoEquiv_trans, conjugateIsoEquiv_isoWhiskerLeft, conjugateIsoEquiv_isoWhiskerRight and conjugateIsoEquiv_associator transport it to Etale.lowerStarComp_assoc, which is stated for any coefficient category and applies to Type (u+1). Take inverse components at F. Finally, prove setPullComp_transport by substituting the equality of scheme arrows; this supplies exactly the eqToHom of Category.assoc in the target statement. All helpers are fully proved, and the arbitrary optional composite arrow allows both bracketings without changing any statement.

split_report.summary: Split the sheaf-of-sets composition and unit statement into five steps following Stacks 03CB/03CC and the small-etale description 021I/021J. The unit is the identity-indexed coprojection followed by sheafification; fibre-product pasting gives the direct-image comparison; composite adjunction and uniqueness of left adjoints give the isomorphism; the local-section description of sheafification proves uniqueness for each fixed sheaf, and that uniqueness plus the unit formulas gives associativity. No new DAG nodes were needed; the cited Lean composition and coherence declarations have abelian coefficients and do not state this sets claim.
